question: How many elements are present in the 7th period of the Modern Periodic table?
solution:
The correct answer is __**32**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The seventh time frame contains **32 components**, tied for the most with period 6, starting with francium and finishing with oganesson, the heaviest component presently found.
 
• The all-out number of electrons that can be obliged in the seventh period is** 2 ( in 7s) + 14(in 5f) + 10(in 6d )+ 6(in 7p) = 32**. The most extreme number of components present in it is 32.
 
• **A period 7 **component is one of the substance components in the seventh column (or time) of the occasional table of the compound components.
 
• Generally speaking, period 7 components fill their **7s shells** first, then, at that point, their** 5f, 6d, and 7p shells** in a specific order, however, there are exemptions, like uranium.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Francium **has the substance image Fr and nuclear number 87.
 
• **Radium **(Ra, nuclear number 88), is a practically unadulterated white basic earth metal, however, it promptly oxidizes, responding with nitrogen (as opposed to oxygen) on openness to air, becoming dark in variety.
 
• **The actinide or actinoid **(IUPAC classification) series envelops the 15 metallic substance components with nuclear numbers from 89 to 103, actinium through lawrencium.
 
• Transactinide components are likewise transuranic components, that is to say, have a nuclear number more noteworthy than that of **uranium (92)**, an actinide.
